children: Shares of SharonAI Holdings jumped 9% in the afternoon session after the company reported third-quarter revenue rose 1,859% year on year and said it expected $400 million to $450 million in annualized run rate revenue (ARR) from January 2027.

According to the company's earnings release, SharonAI Holdings posted revenue of $9.9 million for the third quarter ended September 30, 2026, up 414% from the second quarter of 2026, alongside a net loss of $43.8 million compared with a net loss of $1.6 million in the third quarter of 2025. The release also showed that approximately 30 megawatts (MW) of its 129 MW of contracted capacity is expected to be billing from January 2027, and detailed an approximately $1.0 billion, five-year take-or-pay contract with a global services company, a $170 million, four-year take-or-pay contract with a U.S.-based AI inference platform and data center energization for approximately 8,000 NVIDIA B300 and 4,000 NVIDIA GB300 clusters.

In addition, the company's earnings press release highlighted a $1.32 billion, five-year take-or-pay contract with a global AI lab and the delivery and acceptance of an approximately 1,000 NVIDIA B300 GPU cluster by a global technology company.
What is the market telling us

SharonAI Holdings’s shares are extremely volatile and have had 99 moves greater than 5% over the last year. In that context, today’s move indicates the market considers this news meaningful but not something that would fundamentally change its perception of the business.

The previous big move we wrote about was 1 day ago when the stock dropped 15.3% on the news that the Commerce Department moved to shut down a loophole letting Chinese companies lease Nvidia computing power overseas, intensifying concern that Nvidia's leadership upheaval could curb its financing of server and cloud buildouts ahead of third-quarter earnings later in the week, CNBC reported. Goldman Sachs analyst James Schneider warned in a client note cited by CNBC that new multi-party ecosystem deals may prove harder to negotiate.

Server builders and debt-financed neoclouds rely on uninterrupted GPU allocations, accessible credit, and broad end-user demand to convert backlogs into cash flow. As a result, restricting third-country compute leasing could narrow overseas capacity demand.
SharonAI Holdings is down 25.1% since the beginning of the year, and at $23.74 per share, it is trading below its 52-week high of $139 from December 2025.

Nvidia’s chips cost a hundred grand. The connectors that make them work cost even more. One company makes them all.

Every AI server needs specialized infrastructure the chip companies don’t make. High-speed cables. Power connectors. Thermal sensors. This 90-year-old company built a monopoly on it. The AI boom just started. This stock is still flying under the radar.

title: Why are SharonAI Holdings shares soaring today
